Explain the example for treat network hints as hints

blocks.text: The online and offline events are useful clues. A device can report online even when a particular server cannot be reached.

These examples belong in separate files on your own HTTPS or localhost site. Service workers need that trusted origin and cannot run in this site's sandbox. Use browser developer tools to inspect them.

blocks.code:
window.addEventListener("offline", () => console.log("The browser reports offline."));
window.addEventListener("online", () => console.log("The browser reports online. Try the request again."));
blocks.title: Treat network hints as hints

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `addEventListener` waits for the named event before calling the function you pass to it.

blocks.text: The page can explain a change in connection state. It still needs to catch failures from each real request.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not treat navigator.onLine as proof that every request will succeed.

blocks.text: Compare an offline event with a failed request.
